verified.catalyst: Comcast plans a tax-free spin-off of NBCUniversal and Sky into a separately listed media company. It was announced 2026-06-29 and is expected to close about one year later. Comcast keeps up to a 19.9% stake for up to a year, and each company gets an investment-grade balance sheet.
verified.dated_milestone: Announced 2026-06-29; close targeted ~mid-2027 ("approximately one year"). NEXT: Form 10 filing with the debt-allocation terms and NBCU carve-out financials. No filing or date found as of 2026-11-20; expect H1-2027 (undated). Final board approval and regulatory clearances are still pending.
verified.instrument: CMCSA common (NASDAQ). Later, possibly NBCU when-issued shares once the Form 10 is effective.
verified.bloom_gates: G1 yes (named spinco NBCUniversal+Sky; named CEOs Cavanagh and Angelakis). G2 partial: a public plan with a ~1-year target, but final board approval, regulatory clearance and financing are still conditions. G3 NO: no specific unpriced figure has been disclosed. The split of the >$90B debt pile, NBCU carve-out EBITDA and the retained-stake mechanics are all still unknown, so any upside depends on a multiple re-rating, not a contracted number.
verified.edge: M-L. Run-up from the pre-catalyst base: $23.17 close on 2026-06-26, now $24.86 = +7.3%. The stock spiked to $24.55 on the announcement, then faded to ~$22.9 (50-day average). Remaining capture (my own rough SoP, not an analyst target): about +17% bear ($29), +40% mid ($35), +65% bull ($41) to a provenance-checked value. Most of the event is NOT harvested. But the gain is a sum-of-the-parts re-rating that depends on unknown debt allocation and on cable multiples, which keep compressing as broadband and video losses continue. There is no contractual numerator.
verified.primary_source: Comcast press release 'Comcast Announces Plans to Separate Media and Technology Businesses Into Two Leading Public Companies' (Business Wire, 2026-06-28/29). Comcast Q3-2026 results release (Oct 2026; Zacks/TelecomLead coverage: total debt $87.37B, net debt $76.6B, adj. EBITDA $9.106B, buyback paused through separation). FMP quote $24.86 (2026-11-20) and EOD $23.17 (2026-06-26).
verified.analysis: The spin is real, named and forward: 2026-06-29 announcement (Business Wire), not fired, Form 10 not yet filed. The stock is only +7% above the pre-announcement close, so the residual is mostly unharvested. Numerator provenance: the capital structure has no preferred stock and no external manager. Debt is $87.4B total / ~$76.6B net (Q3-2026 release; net-debt figure from secondary coverage, 10-Q not opened), net leverage 2.3x. EV is about $165B against ~$36B annualized adjusted EBITDA (Q3 $9.1B x4), roughly 4.5x. I re-derived the SoP using assumed segment-EBITDA splits, not reported ones: Connectivity ~$26-27B at 4.5-5.5x plus NBCU/Sky ~$10B at 6-7.5x, less net debt, over ~3.54B shares, gives $29-41. That supports positive equity upside. Score is held at 5 / WATCH because G3 fails: no specific unpriced figure, no dated next milestone, and the value rests on market multiples while Connectivity keeps shrinking (Q3: -144k broadband, -274k video). Gaps: the 10-Q was not opened directly, so the debt and segment-EBITDA splits are unverified. Upgrade when the Form 10 discloses debt allocation and NBCU standalone EBITDA, or when when-issued trading prices the parts.

verified.catalyst: The Dec 29 2026 EGM (2/3 vote) on merging Lux Criteo into Criteo Holdings, Inc. (Delaware). On approval Criteo becomes a US-domiciled company around January 2027 and moves from Nasdaq to NYSE, which makes it eligible for Russell and S&P US indices.
verified.dated_milestone: 2026-12-29 EGM vote (11:00 Luxembourg time). Merger close expected January 2027. Earliest realistic index event: the FTSE Russell 2027 reconstitution (rank day about 2027-04-30, effective late June 2027). The S&P SmallCap 600 is not reachable at today's $0.88B market cap.
verified.instrument: CRTO common (Nasdaq; NYSE after the merger)
verified.bloom_gates: G2 only (concrete commitment): the board approved the merger on 2026-07-29, the DEFM14A sets the vote date, and closing is guided for January 2027. G1 fails because the counterparty is Criteo's own subsidiary and no third party is involved. G3 fails because no specific unpriced figure exists: index buying is an estimated flow, not a contractual number, and no provider has announced an addition or a date.
verified.edge: L-M. Run-up from the pre-catalyst base: about -15% (the US step was board-approved on 2026-07-29 at $22.63 and the 07-28 close was $21.15; today $17.95; the 2026-08-05 drop to $17.05 came with results). So nothing has been harvested on price. Remaining capture is only the flow effect from joining an index, roughly +5-10% at best. That gain is unproven: Russell 2000 entry is plausible at about $0.9B, but the S&P 600 needs about $1.1B+ plus GAAP profitability, the next Russell window is about 7 months away, and the MSCI addition (effective 2026-11-30) has already used up part of the flow story. No figure from the capital structure supports a larger event-driven gain.
verified.primary_source: Criteo S.A. DEFM14A, SEC EDGAR (filed November 2026; vote set for 2026-12-29); 8-K12B dated 2026-07-29 (Luxembourg redomicile done, board approves the US merger, January 2027 close guidance); Form 425 Q&A dated 2026-07-29 (index eligibility not guaranteed); FMP quote dated 2026-11-20 ($17.95, market cap $883M) and FMP end-of-day prices 2026-07-20 to 2026-08-10
verified.analysis: The event checks out and is forward and dated. A DEFM14A sets the vote for Dec 29 2026, the merger needs 2/3, closing is guided for January 2027, and the NYSE move takes effect at completion. The upside the flag calls the real asymmetry is not contractual. Criteo's own Form 425 Q&A says index eligibility is not guaranteed and depends on each provider's methodology. At the current $883M market cap, the S&P SmallCap 600 looks out of reach, which leaves Russell as the realistic route, and its first possible window is the 2027 reconstitution (about June 2027). The stock trades about 15% below its level when the US step was announced, so the event is not priced as a gain. But what is left is a modest, uncertain index-buying effect on top of an equity whose direction depends on its ad-tech fundamentals (which caused the August drop). This makes it a WATCH structural kicker, not an ACTIVE event trade. Gap: I did not confirm the exact FTSE Russell 2027 schedule or the S&P eligibility thresholds against primary sources, and I did not read the 10-Q for the capital structure (Criteo has no preferred stock and is understood to hold net cash, but this was not re-verified).

verified.catalyst: Fertitta Entertainment's $31.00 cash take-private of Caesars closes after the FTC second-request review and the state gaming approvals clear.
verified.dated_milestone: Shareholders approved the deal 2026-09-22 and both sides got an FTC second request 2026-09-14 (still pending). Next date: initial outside date 2027-05-27, which auto-extends to 2027-08-27 and 2027-11-27. A ticking fee of $0.00715/share/day starts 2027-07-01 if the deal has not closed by 2027-06-26. Closing guidance is H1 to mid/late 2027.
verified.bloom_gates: G1 yes (named buyer Fertitta Entertainment, Tilman Fertitta). G2 yes (signed merger agreement, $31.00 cash, no financing condition, 10-bank committed debt, $450M reverse termination fee, shareholder-approved). G3 weak: the remaining figure is only a ~5.9% spread, and it is priced as a duration and regulatory spread, not an unpriced number.
verified.edge: L. Run-up from the unaffected base: the price on 2026-02-25 was ~$20.8 ($31 is a 49% premium to it), so ~+41% has already been captured to $29.27. Remaining: +5.9% to $31.00 (~7-9% annualized for a close between mid and late 2027), plus a small ticking-fee kicker after 2027-06-26. The event is mostly harvested and the spread is plain-vanilla FTC/gaming duration risk. The Icahn $34 bid was rejected, so the market is not pricing a topping bid. Downside if the deal breaks is back toward the low $20s.
verified.primary_source: FMP quote CZR $29.27 (2026-11-20). Caesars/Fertitta merger release 2026-05-28 ($31 cash, 49% premium to the 2026-02-25 unaffected price, $17.6B EV). CDC Gaming / casino.org on the FTC second request (2026-09-14) and the shareholder approval (2026-09-22). iGaming Business on the ticking fee (2026-06-26 trigger) and the $450M reverse termination fee. All trade press; the SEC 8-K was not read directly.
verified.analysis: The deal is real, contractual and dated: a $31 cash Fertitta take-private, shareholder-approved 2026-09-22, with FTC second requests issued 2026-09-14 and multi-state gaming approvals (NV, NJ and others) still outstanding. The numerator is a cash deal price, so no waterfall re-derivation is needed. Residual capture is ~5.9% gross against ~41% already harvested from the unaffected $20.8, and the break risk (FTC remedy or asset sales, gaming-review delays) is asymmetric to the downside. Score is capped at 4 as mostly harvested; it stays a WATCH, and a wider spread or an FTC clearance would be the trigger to re-look. Gap: I did not read the 8-K or the merger agreement directly, and the ticking fee and outside dates come from trade press (iGaming Business, CDC Gaming); I found no news after September 2026.
